newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-Pacific BBA profit seen flat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-Pacific BBA profit seen flat.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd is expected to announce on Tuesday a flat annual profit result of around A$23 million.
Share analysts forecast a net profit of between A$22.6 million and A$25.3 million for calendar 1996, according to a survey by private forecasting service Barcep.
The average of forecasts is A$23.5 million, compared with a pre-abnormal net profit of A$25.3 million in 1995.
The forecasts are roughly in line with the company's own forecast three months ago of a flat result.
Pacific BBA told the stock market in December its automotive division, PBR Automotive, performed much the same as it did in 1995 and margins within its plastics division narrowed.
"The significant increase for them will come in the current year," said analyst David Spry of brokerage F.W. Holst and Co Pty Ltd, citing strong automotive sales growth.

Pacific BBA makes car parts, plastic packaging and products used in construction. Its Banksia park brake products have won major offshore sales contracts, including a recently announced A$200 million, five-deal supply deal into the United States.

Macquarie Equities recently reaffirmed its buy rating on Pacific BBA shares, noting that the PBR Automotive unit would supply product to about 45 percent of General Motors Corp's U.S. domestic car sales by 1998.
Pacific BBA's Webforge engineering unit and its plastics division are both expanding into Asia.
Holst and Co has forecast a leap in pre-abnormal net earnings in 1997, to around A$37 million, and believes there is still "a little bit of value" in the company's share price.
Holst analyst Spry said costs associated with Pacific BBA's expansion had weighed on 1996 earnings.
"It's quite costly, all of this expansion that's required to cater for these contracts. That's the major reason that it's flat, plus the automotive market in Australia," he told Reuters.
Pacific BBA share closed on Monday at A$4.28, down two cents on Friday's close.
